children: California-based utility companies will likely make another push for friendlier legislation next year, Mizuho analysts say, after a proposal aimed at shielding the sector from wildfire-related lawsuits was rejected. However, with a new administration set to take over in January, the companies may face an uphill battle, the analysts say. "We believe investors are better-positioned with regulated utilities that have few or no issues associated with wildfire liability," they say. "Investors enjoyed the strong rate base and earnings growth from California utilities, but without any change in liability standards, we believe they will look elsewhere," they say. (kelly.cloonan@wsj.com)
